# Evaluating AI Research Agents: SwarmEvolve vs. Scientist World

SwarmEvolve reports faster program search, while Scientist World tests research agents on paper-derived environments; the studies answer different questions.

◆ Lena ParkForkast mind|

Two arXiv v1 preprints, SwarmEvolve and Scientist World, measure different research-agent tasks: evolutionary program search and performance in paper-derived environments.

### Throughput and Evolutionary Search ### Throughput and Evolutionary Search

SwarmEvolve, authored by Qile Jiang and George Em Karniadakis, focuses on the efficiency of evolutionary program search. The system operates by deploying 10 swarms, each containing 45 latent agents per round. To maintain diversity, a novelty filter keeps 30 agents in each swarm; summarizers read their KV caches to synthesize candidate programs. This mechanism is tested across 21 mathematical and scientific-computing problems. ### What the Numbers Can Tell Builders

The two papers do not offer competing measurements of one common capability. SwarmEvolve asks how an evolutionary search framework performs on a defined set of program-optimization tasks under fixed model and compute conditions. Scientist World asks whether agents improve reproduced methods or innovate from problem statements in a set of executable research environments. The first includes a throughput measure; the second reports the share of attempts that beat the reproduced methods. A percentage of successful attempts cannot be ranked against programs evaluated per hour as if one were a higher or lower value on the same scale.

### 4. Marketing analytics, next generation technology and social strategies will be the three markers of success for retail CMOs in 2026.

The three are inseparable as consumers look for brands that tell authentic stories using technologies like AI and hyper-personalization to get a clearer picture of the opportunities that lie between intent and action.

Much of the spotlight for 2025 was on how agentic shopping agents upended traditional search. Experts foresee these agents driving even more product discovery and purchases in the coming months, with Forrester research predicting that one-quarter of shoppers will use specialty retail chatbots in 2026. An understanding of just how much retail companies will invest in AI and how they will parcel the capital is nebulous at best. Gartner projects that by the end of 2026, 40% of enterprise applications will include task-specific AI agents. It forecasts that, in a best-case scenario, agentic AI could generate nearly 30% of enterprise application software revenue by 2035.

IDC has reportedthat year-over-year spending on artificial intelligence is expected to grow by 31.9% between 2025 and 2029, fueled by the rise of agentic AI-enabled applications and systems designed to manage fleets of AI agents. Where things get dicey is the potential for these shopping agents to reshape influence away from traditional ad-driven funnels toward AI recommendations. As shoppers rely more heavily on AI agents, brand visibility becomes upended. Whether or not a retailer’s brand shows up will depend on AI optimization — not just SEO or paid ads — flattening long-standing competitive advantages.

Another cautionary note: Guardrails are non-negotiable for safety, compliance and trust. Agentic AI systems act independently, making decisions across multiple steps and integrated systems. That rachets up risk levels. Another potential risk: the possibility that a malicious actor could inject harmful code into an AI platform.

articles.snippet: ##### Abstract The advent of Large Language Models (LLMs) has significantly revolutionized web search. The emergence of LLM-based Search Agents marks a pivotal shift towards deeper, dynamic, autonomous information seeking. These agents can comprehend user intentions and environment context and execute multi-turn retrieval with dynamic planning, extending search capabilities far beyond the web. Leading examples like OpenAI’s Deep Research highlight their potential for deep information mining and real-world applications. This survey provides the first systematic analysis of search agents. We comprehensively analyze and categorize existing works from the perspectives of architecture, optimization, application, and evaluation, ultimately identifying critical open challenges and outlining promising future research directions in this rapidly evolving field.

articles.snippet:
That’s the heart of it. Airlines have spent decades trying to get customers to book directly, where they can sell seat upgrades, bags, and credit cards without paying a middleman. Online travel agencies and comparison sites already sit between airlines and travelers. An AI agent that books for millions of people would be a new, even more powerful middleman, one that could steer you toward whichever airline is cheapest today.

United is keeping the parts of AI that bring it customers, such as fares showing up in AI search, while blocking the part that could take the customer relationship away.

## How Other Airlines Handle AI Agents The new ChatGPT dots and similar always-on agents can still plan a trip from start to finish. They just can’t press the final button on United anymore.

## FAQs

### What is an AI agent?

An AI agent is software that can take actions online for you, such as filling in forms, making purchases, or booking appointments, rather than just answering questions. Many agents work by logging in to websites with your details, which is why companies worry about security and who’s responsible when something goes wrong.

### Can AI agents make payments safely? ## How Other Airlines Handle AI Agents

|  |  |
 --- |
| Airline | Current approach |
| United | Blocks unauthorized agents from booking; may authorize platforms later |
| Delta | Lets agents book if they sign in with your SkyMiles number and password; you’re responsible for what they do |
| American | Still evaluating; some AI tools can already help buy American tickets |
| Southwest | Made its flight inventory viewable to ChatGPT users |
| easyJet | Offers booking and flight-status tracking inside the ChatGPT app |

The split is clear. Delta, Southwest and easyJet are letting AI in on their own terms, either by accepting logins with clear responsibility or by building official integrations. United is the first major US carrier to reject third-party AI travel planners outright.

articles.title: Agentic AI strategy | Deloitte Insights
articles.snippet: Legacy system integration: Traditional enterprise systems weren’t designed for agentic interactions. Most agents still rely on application programming interfaces (APIs) and conventional data pipelines to access enterprise systems, which creates bottlenecks and limits their autonomous capabilities. Gartner predicts that over 40% of agentic AI projects will fail by 2027 because legacy systems can’t support modern AI execution demands. These systems lack the real-time execution capability, modern APIs, modular architectures, and secure identity management needed for true agentic integration.4 The solution involves a paradigm shift from traditional data pipelines to what can be described as enterprise search and indexing—similar to how Google made the World Wide Web discoverable. This approach involves contextualizing enterprise data through content and index stores built on knowledge graphs, making information discoverable without requiring extensive ETL processes. Data architecture constraints: Current enterprise data architectures, built around extract, transform, load (ETL) processes and data warehouses, create friction for agent deployment. The fundamental issue is that most organizational data isn’t positioned to be consumed by agents that need to understand business context and make decisions. In a 2025 Deloitte survey, nearly half of organizations cited searchability of data (48%) and reusability of data (47%) as challenges to their AI automation strategy.5

### What are AI search engines for agents?

AI search engines for agents are tools that let your AI agent retrieve fresh, structured web data programmatically. Unlike consumer search engines built for human browsing, they return machine-readable results with optional content extraction, citations, and filtering, designed to drop directly into LLM reasoning loops.

### How do AI search engines for agents differ from Google or Perplexity?

Consumer AI search engines like Perplexity and Google are optimized for human browsing: they return formatted pages, ads, and conversational answers. AI search engines for agents are optimized for code: they return structured JSON, support batch queries, offer fine-grained source filters, and are priced per API call. top10.snippet: ##### Abstract The advent of Large Language Models (LLMs) has significantly revolutionized web search. The emergence of LLM-based Search Agents marks a pivotal shift towards deeper, dynamic, autonomous information seeking. These agents can comprehend user intentions and environment context and execute multi-turn retrieval with dynamic planning, extending search capabilities far beyond the web. Leading examples like OpenAI’s Deep Research highlight their potential for deep information mining and real-world applications. This survey provides the first systematic analysis of search agents. We comprehensively analyze and categorize existing works from the perspectives of architecture, optimization, application, and evaluation, ultimately identifying critical open challenges and outlining promising future research directions in this rapidly evolving field.
